mechanism_narrative: If WORKPLACES and TRANSIT stop falling and begin to recover, weekday foot traffic should spill into discretionary shopping and dining, lifting RETAIL_REC over the next four weeks. The effect is strongest when RESIDENTIAL does not rise at the same time, because fewer people staying home preserves out-of-home spending.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC declines over the next 28 days even though WORKPLACES and TRANSIT each rise from their current levels and RESIDENTIAL does not increase materially.

mechanism_narrative: A further decline in TRANSIT of more than 2 points week-on-week signals weaker city access and fewer incidental shopping trips, which should push RETAIL_REC lower within one to two weeks. The signal fails if retail activity holds up while transit continues to weaken.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC is flat or higher over the next 14 days despite a week-on-week TRANSIT drop larger than 2 points.

mechanism_narrative: When GROCERY_PHARM stays positive while PARKS remain deeply negative, household trip budgets are likely being absorbed by necessities rather than leisure, leaving less capacity for retail-and-recreation visits. Over four weeks this composition should keep RETAIL_REC below its recent average.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC rises above its last-4-week mean even though GROCERY_PHARM remains positive and PARKS remain strongly negative.

mechanism_narrative: In a tightening-restrictions regime, stable or rising RESIDENTIAL mobility indicates more time spent at home and fewer discretionary outings, so RETAIL_REC should fall over the next month. The mechanism fails if people stay home more but retail mobility does not soften.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not decline over the next 28 days while RESIDENTIAL remains at or above its current level.

mechanism_narrative: If PARKS mobility rebounds by more than 3 points from one week to the next, it marks a leisure reallocation that usually competes with shopping center visits and cafe traffic. Under that condition RETAIL_REC should weaken within the next two weeks.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC fails to fall within 14 days after a PARKS increase greater than 3 points.

mechanism_narrative: A joint recovery in TRANSIT and WORKPLACES signals a broader return of commuting density, which should raise nearby retail visits and shopping add-ons over the next four weeks. The effect is conditional on GROCERY_PHARM not surging, because a necessity-only trip mix would not translate into discretionary retail gains.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC remains below its last-4-week mean even though TRANSIT and WORKPLACES rise together and GROCERY_PHARM does not increase materially.

mechanism_narrative: If RESIDENTIAL falls while WORKPLACES rises, households are reallocating time from home to outside activity, a pattern that should lift retail-and-recreation spending within one week. The signal is short-lived and should appear first in the weekly mean immediately after the crossover.
candidate_trigger: RESIDENTIAL falls below its prior week while WORKPLACES rises above its prior week
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not increase within 7 days after RESIDENTIAL drops and WORKPLACES rises in the same week.

mechanism_narrative: If TRANSIT stays near its current deeply negative level and WORKPLACES remain suppressed, the city is still operating under constrained movement, which should keep retail-and-recreation below the last month’s average over the next four weeks. This mechanism breaks if mobility restrictions ease enough to restore commuting flow without a retail response.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC rises above its last-28-day mean while TRANSIT and WORKPLACES both remain materially below baseline.
